subject.title: fix(backup): sweep stale temp artifacts before creating new backup

question: Should `backup create` delete stale OpenClaw-owned backup temp artifacts after a guarded grace window once the timestamped-output matcher is fixed?
rationale: The code defect is mechanical, but automatic deletion of old backup artifacts is an operator-visible cleanup policy that maintainers should explicitly own before merge.

options.title: Accept guarded startup cleanup after matcher fix
options.body: Broaden the matcher, keep owner and age guards tight, and treat stale partial backup artifacts as disposable crash cleanup.

options.title: Limit cleanup to stable file outputs
options.body: Accept a narrower behavior that protects fixed `--output <file>` paths but leaves default and directory-output archive temps to external cleanup.

options.title: Reject startup deletion policy
options.body: Pause or close this PR and document external janitor cleanup instead of making backup startup delete stale artifacts.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded startup cleanup after matcher fix
recommendation.body: Broaden the matcher, keep owner and age guards tight, and treat stale partial backup artifacts as disposable crash cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently maintained the current backup file shape and owned the adjacent memory stale-temp cleanup precedent with live-owner guards.
